# DateTime

A date and a time of day together, in some understood offset.

```rux
pub struct DateTime {
    pub date: Date;
    pub time: TimeOfDay;
}
```

`Copy`. What offset the pair is in is the caller's knowledge, carried beside it where it matters — attaching
one permanently would make every arithmetic answer depend on a field that is usually UTC anyway.

## Fields

| Name   | Type        | Description         |
| ------ | ----------- | ------------------- |
| `date` | `Date`      | The day.            |
| `time` | `TimeOfDay` | The time within it. |

## Methods

<h3 id="to-timestamp"><code>ToTimestamp</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ToTimestamp(self: &DateTime, offset: UtcOffset) -> Timestamp
```

The moment this date and time name in UTC, shifted by `offset`.
The shift subtracts: half past nine at plus two is half past seven in UTC. The range of a timestamp dwarfs
the calendar's, so the conversion cannot overflow for any date [`Date::New`](/docs/api/time/date#new) accepts.

| Name     | Type        | Description         |
| -------- | ----------- | ------------------- |
| `offset` | `UtcOffset` | the offset from UTC |

**Returns**: the moment this local time names at that offset

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Calendar.rux#L242)

<h3 id="equals"><code>Equals</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Equals(self: &DateTime, other: DateTime) -> bool
```

Whether two pairs name the same date and time.
Same field values — two pairs in different offsets naming one moment are different here, which is what
carrying the offset beside the pair means.

| Name    | Type       | Description                  |
| ------- | ---------- | ---------------------------- |
| `other` | `DateTime` | the value to compare against |

**Returns**: whether the two are the same

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Calendar.rux#L279)

## Implements Display

`DateTime` conforms to `Display`.

<h3 id="write-display"><code>WriteDisplay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDisplay(self: &DateTime, writer: &var TextWriter, spec: FormatSpec) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes the local date and time as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, with no offset.
The absence is deliberate and is the point of the type. A [`DateTime`](/docs/api/time/date-time) holds no offset, so writing one would
mean inventing it: `Z` would claim UTC and the machine's local offset would claim a place, and both would
be a guess presented as a fact. [`OffsetDateTime`](/docs/api/time/offset-date-time) is the type that has somewhere to keep an offset, and it
is what produces RFC 3339.
Reports whatever the writer reported, `UnsupportedRequest` for a style other than `iso8601` or `rfc3339`,
and `UnsupportedRequest` for a precision past nine.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole date and time were accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Calendar.rux#L259)

## Related

<h3 id="parse-date-time"><code>ParseDateTime</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ParseDateTime(text: char8[..]) -> DateTime ! TimeParseError
```

Reads `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.fraction]`, with no offset.
The separator may be `T`, `t` or a space, which is as far as the RFC 3339 liberality goes. No offset is read,
and one present is text after the value: a [`DateTime`](/docs/api/time/date-time) has nowhere to keep an offset, so accepting one would
discard it silently. [`ParseRfc3339`](/docs/api/time/offset-date-time#parse-rfc3339) is what reads a moment that carries one.
The failures [`ParseDate`](/docs/api/time/date#parse-date) and [`ParseTimeOfDay`](/docs/api/time/time-of-day#parse-time-of-day) report, at their offsets within this text.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/CalendarParse.rux#L261)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type        | Description      |
| ------ | ----------- | ---------------- |
| `text` | `char8[..]` | the text to read |

**Returns**: the local date and time, or why the text is not one
